history.dynasty: Pallava (one travel source says built by Mahendra Varman - weakly sourced, verify); Chera-Chola-Pandya era (Tevaram-period antiquity); medieval Getti Mudaliyars (contributions per grokipedia - verify)
history.period: Ancient; glorified in the 7th-century Tevaram of Tirugnana Sambandar - one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams; last major kumbhabhishekam 10 September 2000 per grokipedia
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Erode town - it stands at Kooduthurai in Bhavani town, about 15 km from Erode city (CSV town 'Erode' refers to the district; corrected to Bhavani). Documented with the corrected location. The Sangameswarar Temple is the great Shiva shrine of Bhavani at the Dakshina Triveni Sangamam - the confluence of the Kaveri, the Bhavani and the mystic subterranean Amutha (Agaya Gangai). Ancient names: Thirunana (praised in old Tamil literature), Thirukooduthurai/Kooduthurai, Mukkoodal/Mukkudal (joining of the three), Dakshina Prayag. Sthala purana: Sage Parasara hid a little of the churning-of-the-ocean amrit for the world's welfare; four asuras tried to steal it and Shiva drove them off; when Parasara tried to retrieve the pot he found a swayambhu lingam inside, and lifting it released a jet of water (the Amutha) that joined the Kaveri and Bhavani - as the Lord was found at this sangam (confluence), He is Sangameswarar. Kubera legend: flying over the Cauvery he saw deer, tiger, cow, elephant, snake and rat drinking together in peace near an Ilandhai tree; a divine voice told him this was a place the Vedas visited, and bid him worship the lingam under the tree (the sthala vriksham, an Ilandhai/Zizyphus tree that fruits in all seasons). The shrine is one of the seven prominent Shiva temples of Kongu Nadu and the Bhaskara Kshetram (sun god worshipped Shiva here); Sambandar composed 10 Tevaram hymns here (2nd Thirumurai) and Arunagirinathar sang Thirupugazh on Subramanya. In 1804 the British Collector of Coimbatore, William Garrow (Karo), was miraculously saved from a collapsing bungalow by a girl the priest identified as Vedanayaki Amman; he bore three holes in the temple wall opposite her shrine to pray through, and presented her a golden cot/cradle on 11-1-1804 - one source says a gold plate with his signature (CONFLICT on the gift's exact form - verify). Bhavani is a Parihara Sthalam; devotees perform last rites on the riverbank where the Kaveri flows north-to-south. The 4-acre complex has a five-tiered rajagopuram facing north, shrines facing east, an 18-pillar nritya mantapam, and the famous paired stone statues before the Ambal sannidhi - one smiles, one sheds tears when milk or water is poured on them (per Wikipedia - verify). A separate Vishnu shrine (with the cow behind the Vishnu statue) marks Saiva-Vaishnava harmony; every inch under the temple is said to hold a lingam.

name: Sangameswarar Temple
town: Bhavani (CSV town 'Erode' is WRONG - the temple is in Bhavani town at Kooduthurai, ~15 km from Erode city)
town_description: Bhavani is a sacred town in Erode district at the confluence of the Kaveri and Bhavani rivers (with the invisible Amutha), known as the Triveni Sangam of the South. The Sangameswarar Temple stands on the northern bank at Kooduthurai. Beyond the temple, Bhavani is a weaving centre famous for the Bhavani Jamakkalam carpet industry, and was ruled in turn by Cheras, Cholas and Vijayanagara.
